conviction_note: Fundamentals lean to another beat (Q3 carries the 'significant' hyperscale DirectFlash revenue at 75-85% margins the company promised, and P has beaten its own guide three quarters running), and the stock arrives de-rated (-26% in 20 days on a sector-wide AI-hardware selloff, bullish sentiment 22%) with calls bid. Against that, P sold all three prints under its current name, including a $500M+ FY raise, and one source puts FY27 consensus at $5.29B, above the $5.07B top of the guide, so the market needs a large raise. So the findings sum to a small positive (+1.4) while p_up sits at 51 on a 14-point scale. The scaled number (+0.28) is far smaller than the sum because the reaction function has sold every beat.
bar: Q3 FY27 company guide: revenue $1.325-1.335B, non-GAAP operating profit $265-275M (Q2 FY27 prepared remarks, https://s21.q4cdn.com/687136699/files/doc_financials/2027/q2/Q2FY27-Prepared-Remarks.pdf). Sell-side Q3 consensus is disputed. One reading is $1.33B revenue / $0.77 EPS with a $0.81 whisper (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/P/23139, https://finviz.com/news/420784/everpure-must-prove-its-guidance-leap-is-real-as-cash-flow-snap-back-faces-test). Chartmill/FXEmpire show about $1.36B and $0.78 (per a search snippet). FY27 guide is $5.03-5.07B, reaffirmed at the Sept 24 analyst day. Earnings Whispers alone puts FY27 consensus at $5.29B, above the guide. Preliminary FY28 outlook is $7.0-7.3B against a $6.2B consensus. The revenue bar is sized against the company guide, and findings that depend on the FY consensus are capped small because it has one source.
positioning_check: Short interest 9.10M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (+0.93M from the prior period), days to cover 1.91 (https://equibles.com/stocks/p/short-interest, FINRA data). That is roughly 3% of float, so the short is not crowded, and no November settlement was found. 25-delta skew is -6.79 vol points, so calls are paid and the priced lean is upside. ATM IV is 214%, put/call OI 0.72, and the event-implied move 14.33%. The stock is -26.1% over 20 days and -38% from its 52-week high ($157.57 on Oct 13). Bullish sentiment fell from 48% to about 22% (Earnings Whispers).

findings.finding: Everpure told investors at Q2 (Aug 26) to expect 'significant hyperscale product revenue in Q3 and Q4, based on order commitments through the Hyperscalers' Supply Chain'. It said hyperscale deployments carry 75-85% gross margins against a core product GM of 66.2%, so the quarter that ended Nov 1 is the first with a real hyperscale contribution and should lift product gross margin, which the market reads as stuck at the low end of 65-70%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 product GM rose 70bp sequentially to 66.2% and the stock still fell 8.87%. All three prints under the Everpure name were sold (-10.3, -14.81, -8.87).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 guide already includes this. Previews (Earnings Whispers, finviz Nov 10) describe margins as 'slipping toward 65%' and do not model a hyperscale mix uplift. If the uplift were priced, previews would carry a product-GM step-up and the skew would not need to pay for calls. It lands inside the company guide, so the size is small.
findings.independence: Meta narrowed its 2026 capex up to $135-145B on Oct 21 (https://letsdatascience.com/news/meta-narrows-2026-capital-spending-range-to-135-billion-145-46f12e07). Meta is the first hyperscale DirectFlash customer, but this is a proxy and it shares no document with the finding.

findings.finding: Operating cash flow was -$136M and FCF -$238M in Q2 because of NAND and component stockpiling. The CFO said OCF would 'normalize over the next two quarters' and reaffirmed FY27 FCF of $600-800M. With H1 FCF at about -$126M, H2 needs roughly $730-930M, so Q3 FCF is the first check. The inventory was bought ahead of further price rises (TrendForce still sees enterprise SSD contract prices +15-20% in 4Q26), so it funds visible demand and is not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 FCF swing to -$238M coincided with the -8.87% reaction, and Trefis and finviz both name cash flow as the test for this print.
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview flags that the snap-back is unproven, so the market holds this as an open risk and not as an expected recovery. A priced recovery would show as previews treating the $600-800M guide as safe. The answer to 'what does the money buy' is inventory for a +38% revenue ramp, so the sign is a small positive with wide variance.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (the Q2 prepared remarks), so the two are not independent. Trefis (https://www.trefis.com/stock/p/articles/624872/everpure-down-22-what-would-its-ceo-say/2026-11-13) frames the same test.

findings.finding: P beat the top of its own guidance in Q2 (revenue +38% YoY, 5.8% above consensus, op profit +77% to $230M above the guide's high end). Management said it had 'two quarters of visibility' when it set the $1.325-1.335B Q3 guide. A repeat of the Q2 margin would put Q3 revenue near $1.38-1.40B, about 3-5% above the $1.33B consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: P beat three times and fell three times: Q2 FY27 beat with a $500M+ FY raise and fell 8.87%, Q1 FY27 beat and fell 14.81%, Q4 FY26 fell 10.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The $0.81 whisper sits above the $0.77 consensus, so part of the beat is expected. The disputed $1.36B Chartmill figure shows some estimates already sit above the guide. Beats have been sold every time, so the fact is not the reaction. Kept small.
findings.independence: Q2 prepared remarks (https://s21.q4cdn.com/687136699/files/doc_financials/2027/q2/Q2FY27-Prepared-Remarks.pdf) confirm the Q2 guide beat. That is the company's own document.

findings.finding: Earnings Whispers puts FY27 revenue consensus at $5.29B, about $220M above the top of the reaffirmed $5.03-5.07B guide. Q1+Q2+Q3 guide is about $3.52B, so the guide implies a Q4 of about $1.51-1.55B, while that consensus implies about $1.77B. If the figure is right, the stock needs a large Q4 and FY raise just to meet the street, and a routine raise would read as a disappointment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's large FY raise (+$590M at the midpoint) was still sold, falling 8.87%. Guidance is the line this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: If this bar were priced, the stock would not be at 144x trailing P/E with calls bid. On the other hand, a 38% drawdown from the October high may already have removed it. The $5.29B has one source, and finviz repeats the same Earnings Whispers text, so it is capped small. It may also be a data artefact, because the same source puts FY28 consensus ($6.2B) below the company's $7.0-7.3B target.
findings.independence: finviz (https://finviz.com/news/420784/everpure-must-prove-its-guidance-leap-is-real-as-cash-flow-snap-back-faces-test) repeats the same text, so it is not independent. The 247wallst Sept 27 piece (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/27/everpures-7-billion-forecast-just-blew-past-wall-streets-numbers/) gives FY28 consensus as $6.14B, which cuts the other way on the forward bar.

findings.finding: TrendForce's Oct 30 update cut its 4Q26 enterprise SSD contract-price increase to 15-20% QoQ from the 23-28% it forecast on Sept 24. NAND cost inflation is decelerating, which supports management's stated path from the low end of the 65-70% product GM range back toward the high end 'once semiconductor costs begin to stabilize'. It also makes the inventory P stockpiled in Q2 margin-friendly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NAND cost commentary drove the prior selloffs: the April 2026 customer letter on 70% price rises (stock -3.3%), and the Q2 margin worry (-8.87%).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews still frame margins as at risk from cost inflation 'not seen since 2017'. Pricing in a slowdown would show up as previews modelling GM recovery in the Q4 guide. This is an industry proxy, and the company has not confirmed the transmission, so it is small. Slower NAND inflation could also slow P's price-led revenue growth.
findings.independence: Kioxia's November results commentary shows price-rise momentum slowing (https://xenospectrum.com/en/kioxia-guidance-yen-nand-price/, per a search snippet). Proxy.

findings.finding: The 20-day -26% move has no company cause. It tracks a sector-wide AI-hardware selloff: on Nov 5 SanDisk fell 22.3%, Micron 17.5% and WDC/Seagate about 16-17% with NetApp and HPE down; on Nov 12-13 a second leg followed the Nvidia CEO's resignation. The stock arrives de-rated, near its 200-day moving average (about $95), with bullish sentiment at 22%, short interest about 3% of float, and calls paid (skew -6.79).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: All three prior Everpure-named prints came after the stock had run up, and all three were sold. This is the first print to arrive after a drawdown of this size.
findings.why_not_priced: This agrees with the skew (calls paid), so it is partly priced. The run-up argument is that previous prints were sold from extended levels, and a de-rated stock with low sentiment sells a beat less. Unexplained drawdowns are worth little on their own, but this one has a named sector cause, so a beat can unwind part of it.
findings.independence: Trefis on P itself (https://www.trefis.com/stock/p/articles/624872/everpure-down-22-what-would-its-ceo-say/2026-11-13): -22.2% from Oct 14 to Nov 12 with no company trigger. Sector coverage from Motley Fool (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/13/why-sandisk-stock-is-falling-today/).

findings.finding: Meta, the first hyperscale DirectFlash customer, narrowed its 2026 capex range upward to $135-145B (from $130-145B) on Oct 21. That implies Q4 capex of about $49-59B and says investment will stay aggressive into 2027. A direct customer reconfirmed its spending after P last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured P reaction to hyperscaler capex. The Aug 10 second-hyperscaler win took the stock to a 52-week high.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and four weeks old, and the AI-hardware selloff since then suggests the market discounted capex durability anyway. Transmission to P's Q4 hyperscale revenue is inference, so the size is small.

outside_window.finding: The second top-five hyperscaler (TD Cowen suggests Oracle) contributes 'de minimis' revenue in FY27, and the meaningful ramp starts in FY28. The FY28 $7.0-7.3B preliminary outlook resolves over the coming year.

baseline_tension: Upside lean, small. The findings agree with the call-paid skew (-6.79) and lean against the -26% 20-day run-up, which here reads as sector beta and not company-specific disappointment. The 0-for-3 reaction history on beats, plus a possibly elevated FY bar, keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: L1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): P sold 3 of 3 beats, so the hyperscale-GM finding went 0.8 to 0.4 (it also lands inside the guide, L6) and the beat-pattern finding 0.7 to 0.3.
L6 (verify the bar): the Q3 revenue consensus is disputed ($1.33B vs $1.36B) and the FY27 $5.29B has one source, so the FY-bar finding was capped from -1.5 to -1.0.
L4 (financing is a question): the stockpile funds visible demand, so the FCF finding stays positive but goes 0.5 to 0.3 because it lands inside the company's FCF guide.
L5 (proxies are small): the TrendForce NAND finding went 0.5 to 0.4 and Meta capex 0.3 to 0.2.
L7 (positioning): the positioning finding agrees with the skew and is partly priced, 1.0 to 0.8; short interest is not crowded.
